title: Promoted Listings and Seller Tools: Which Ones Actually Move Product

facts.fact: The article was published on 17 August 2026 and carries a 6-minute read time.
The author suggests starting ad rates at roughly half of the platform's suggested rate on a batch of listings.
facts.quote: start at roughly half the suggested rate on a batch of listings and watch for two weeks

facts.fact: The author suggests watching a reduced ad rate for about two weeks before changing it.
facts.quote: start at roughly half the suggested rate on a batch of listings and watch for two weeks

facts.fact: In the author's illustration, ad fees of four percent and thirteen percent stack on top of other seller fees.
facts.quote: Four percent here and thirteen percent there feels small individually

facts.fact: The author recommends sending watcher offers with a modest discount of five to ten percent and a short expiry.
facts.quote: send a modest discount, five to ten percent, with a short expiry

facts.fact: The author says acceptance of watcher offers often jumps at a discount somewhere around eight to twelve percent.
facts.quote: often somewhere around eight to twelve percent, where acceptance jumps

facts.fact: The author advises waiting one week after a listing goes live before sending it offers.
facts.quote: Give a listing a week to find its audience at full price.

facts.fact: The author recommends focusing sharing on the top thirty items by likes plus the newest inventory.
facts.quote: Focus on your top thirty items by likes and your newest inventory.

facts.fact: The author recommends batching sharing into two short daily blocks.
facts.quote: Sharing is worth batching into two short daily blocks rather than spreading across the day.

facts.fact: The author says a listing up for ninety days with steady views and no sales needs a lower price or better photos rather than a relist.
facts.quote: A listing that has been up for ninety days with steady views and no sales does not need a fresh start
